text: 🇲🇽🎨 "During the neoliberal period, some of the polytechnics were built practically as public-private partnerships. And we are now building, from the Fourth Transformation, more public universities and high schools." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 16, 2026 After the Metropolitan Autonomous University, no new public university was built in Mexico City until López Obrador founded the UACM. As president he created the Benito Juárez Well-Being Universities: more than 200 campuses and close to 200,000 students, with medicine among the most demanded degrees. Sheinbaum made the Rosario Castellanos university national: 28 new academic units this year in 20 states, 122,000 students, 63% of them women.

🇲🇽🔍 "When Calderón comes in, there were 24 homicides. When he leaves, he leaves 70 homicides a day." "When Peña arrives, he receives that number. When he leaves, he leaves 100 homicides a day. [...] And with us, half of what there was in 2018." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 16, 2026 A reporter cited displacement in Sásabe, Sonora, and security concerns around pollsters and the Sonora River cleanup. Sheinbaum put the national series on screen: homicides rose with the war on drugs under Calderón, kept climbing under Peña Nieto, and began falling under López Obrador. High-impact crimes went from 636 a day in October 2024 to 408 in September 2026, down 36%. INEGI's survey shows the share of people who feel unsafe in their neighborhood fell from 40.5% to 35.9% in a year. "We have never said everything is solved."

🇲🇽🎨 "What was Casa Tlalpan, the house of the police chief, was a monument to corruption. Today it becomes a university and a high school." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 16, 2026 The estate was built in the 1970s at the foot of the Ajusco for Arturo "El Negro" Durazo, Mexico City's police chief: a main house, discotheque, helipads, stables, a bullring, casino, shooting range, two artificial lakes and a hall for collector cars, on more than 6 hectares. It was recovered by the state in the late 1990s. The Institute to Return to the People What Was Stolen (INDEP) now hands it to the Rosario Castellanos National University and a National High School focused on the arts. 3,067 people registered in the first call, in July. Investment is about 150 million pesos.

🇲🇽✊ "We were first place in the world. Incredible. And I think we dropped to eighth place." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 16, 2026 On Tuesday the Supreme Court upheld the ban on selling junk food in schools, universities included. Sheinbaum said the rate of children with obesity has dropped. The ban comes with the Vive Saludable, Vive Feliz program: IMSS and the Education Ministry visited almost every public primary school and checked the children. Parents get a report with what was found. Children who need glasses get them free, and children with cavities or weight problems are referred to a health center. A new round of visits comes next year.

🇲🇽🏭 "Exports of electronics have increased a lot, and plants are expanding in Mexico." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 16, 2026 The UN Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (ECLAC) projects that Mexican exports will grow 26% this year, above the regional average and above Brazil and Argentina. Sheinbaum said demand for data centers in the United States is driving new electronics plants in Mexico. Part of the auto industry has recovered despite Trump's tariffs, and markets in Europe and Japan have opened beyond the US.

🇲🇽⚖️ "I never instruct the Supreme Court, because it is another branch and I respect the autonomy of the Court. [...] It would be very wrong, it would be illegal." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 16, 2026 A reporter suggested that the president now controls the Court, which was elected by popular vote in 2025. Sheinbaum answered that the branches coordinate on some issues but she gives the Court no instructions. In the same exchange the reporter questioned whom she meets with. She listed farmers, teachers' unions, searching mothers and Indigenous peoples. "If what you want to say is that I only meet with big business, like the PRIAN, you can say it, but it is not true. [...] We live in a democratic country."

🔥🇲🇽 "We are also about to hand over the 200 million pesos recovered from García Luna, from the corruption frauds of García Luna, to the schools of the Montaña of Guerrero." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 16, 2026 Genaro García Luna was Calderón's security minister during the war on drugs. A US jury convicted him in 2023 of taking bribes from the Sinaloa cartel. Part of the money from his corruption frauds has been recovered in Mexico. The Institute to Return to the People What Was Stolen (INDEP) also sends the proceeds of its auctions of seized goods to the Pension Fund for Well-Being and to the government's social programs. Sheinbaum announced a full INDEP report in a coming mañanera.

🇲🇽🛒 <u>Mexican Spending Bounces Back After the World Cup Slump</u>

Mexican household consumption rose 0.4% in August, according to INEGI's timely private consumption indicator reported by El Economista, after a 0.5% drop in June and a flat July, the World Cup months. Year on year, spending is up 0.9% in August and 0.6% in September, when INEGI estimates a 0.1% monthly dip. The full August figures come out November 5.

🇲🇽🎶 <u>Los Tigres del Norte Take the Migrant Anthem to NPR's Tiny Desk</u>

Weeks before the US midterms, Los Tigres del Norte made their NPR Tiny Desk debut and opened with "Somos más americanos," their song about the abuses Mexicans suffer crossing the border and a defense of the migrants who work in the United States. The line everyone knows: "somos más americanos que todititos los gringos." Tiny Desk's producers were moved to tears.
